investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
investigations.description: FLEX studied flame extinguishment of heptane and other liquid fuels in microgravity using the Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus inside the Combustion Integrated Rack.
objectives: Measure extinction limits of liquid fuel droplets in microgravity
Determine effect of oxygen concentration on flame stability
key_findings: Radiative extinction observed at low strain rates
Low-stretch flames can extinguish without suppression
Extinction boundaries mapped across O₂ and pressure
investigations.earth_application: Improved fine-water-mist fire suppression systems and combustion models.
investigations.si_summary: FLEX is the definitive database for liquid-fuel extinction in microgravity, giving lunar habitat designers a calibrated envelope.

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2
investigations.description: FLEX-2 extended FLEX with soot formation measurements and cool-flame detection in heptane droplet flames at varying ambient conditions.
objectives: Measure soot volume fraction in droplet flames
Extend extinction maps to lower pressures
key_findings: Soot formation suppressed below 8 psi
Cool flames observed in droplet wake at low O₂
Extended extinction maps down to 8 psi
investigations.si_summary: FLEX-2 closes the low-pressure gap FLEX left open — critical for lunar habitat design at 10.2 psi.

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
investigations.description: BASS investigated the burning and extinguishment of solid fuels in microgravity, focusing on airflow and oxygen effects on flame spread over spacecraft materials.
objectives: Characterize flame spread over solid materials
Quantify minimum airflow for sustained combustion
Test extinguishment strategies for solid fuel fires
key_findings: Microgravity flames spread slower but more resilient
Low-speed opposed flow sustains flames
Water mist effective when properly directed
investigations.si_summary: BASS established boundary conditions for flame spread over spacecraft materials — the single most important precursor for ISS fire detection.

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
investigations.description: BASS-II expanded BASS to a wider airflow range and additional fuel materials, including cotton blends and fiberglass.
key_findings: Cotton blends propagate faster than PMMA
Extinction limits vary significantly by material
Water mist effectiveness depends on droplet size
investigations.si_summary: BASS-II extended BASS to realistic cabin materials and closed the geometry gap between lab samples and actual spacecraft interiors.

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-I
investigations.description: Saffire-I studied large-scale fire growth in a spacecraft-like environment inside an uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle.
key_findings: Flame growth limits reached in minutes
Significant CO and soot production detected
Smoke detectors must handle low-velocity transport
investigations.si_summary: Saffire-I is the anchor large-scale dataset for spacecraft fire safety. Its CO/soot data feed detector placement for ISS and future vehicles.

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II
investigations.description: Saffire-II tested nine different spacecraft materials in a single large-scale microgravity burn, providing comparative flammability data.
objectives: Extend combustion models to varied fuels
key_findings: Cotton blends propagate fastest; fiberglass slowest
Material ranking differs from Earth-based tests
Soot yield varies 5x across materials
investigations.si_summary: Saffire-II's comparative material dataset is directly load-bearing for spacecraft material selection standards (NASA-STD-6001).

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-III
investigations.description: Saffire-III repeated large-scale burns with varied flow conditions to study flame spread over SIBAL cloth with controlled opposed flow.
objectives: Study flame spread with controlled flow
Measure soot and CO under varied conditions
key_findings: Opposed flow strongly affects spread rate
Soot yield highest at low-flow conditions
Model validation improved with new data
investigations.si_summary: Saffire-III provides the cleanest large-scale flow-controlled fire data, directly improving FDS simulation accuracy for spacecraft.

investigations.name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction
investigations.description: SAME studied ignition, flame spread, and extinction of solid fuels at varying oxygen and pressure, focused on low-pressure high-oxygen habitats.
objectives: Determine flammability boundaries for habitat materials
Provide data for low-pressure habitat design
key_findings: Ignition energy drops dramatically above 30% O₂
Low-pressure high-O₂ equals or worse than 1-atm air
Extinction limits shift measurably with pressure
investigations.si_summary: SAME is the closest existing dataset to lunar habitat fire-safety conditions, quantifying how lower pressure and elevated oxygen change ignition.

investigations.name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction - Reflight
investigations.description: SAME-R expanded SAME with additional material types and extended test matrix for Artemis-era material screening.
key_findings: Nomex shows 40% lower ignition energy at 32% O₂
Kevlar blends sustain flame at low flow above 30% O₂
Lunar-spec thresholds now empirically defined
investigations.si_summary: SAME-R is the single closest investigation to lunar habitat conditions, testing directly at 32% O₂ — the Artemis spec.

investigations.name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator
investigations.description: ACME-BRE measured burning rates of solid and liquid fuels in microgravity, focusing on emulating realistic material burning under controlled conditions.
objectives: Measure burning rates across fuel types
key_findings: Burning rate non-monotonic vs airflow speed
Solid and liquid converge at high airflow
Recalibrates spacecraft fire models
investigations.si_summary: ACME-BRE delivers the burning-rate table that every downstream spacecraft fire model needs.

investigations.name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Cool Flames Investigation
investigations.description: ACME-CFI extended cool-flame studies to a wider range of gaseous fuels and high oxygen concentrations, targeting detection of incipient fires.
objectives: Extend cool-flame maps to blended fuels
key_findings: Cool flames exist up to 75% O₂
Blends broaden cool-flame regime
Detection requires multiple sensor modalities
investigations.si_summary: ACME-CFI is the second-highest O₂ investigation in this set, directly informing lunar habitat detection systems at 30%+ oxygen.

investigations.name: Cool Flames Investigation - Gaseous Fuels
investigations.description: CFI-G explored low-temperature 'cool flame' combustion in microgravity, including tests up to 85% O₂ to map low-temperature reaction pathways.
objectives: Measure ignition and extinction at 85% O₂
key_findings: Cool flames observed at high O₂
Multiple regimes coexist
High-O₂ ignition sensitive to temperature
investigations.si_summary: CFI-G is the only investigation in this set testing up to 85% O₂ — the highest relevance for lunar habitats and pressurized suits.

investigations.name: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
investigations.description: SPICE investigated structure and liftoff of non-buoyant jet flames in microgravity, providing insight into flame stability obscured by buoyancy on Earth.
key_findings: Liftoff limits shift from Earth values
Flame shape measurably different from 1-g
Data improve detection thresholds
investigations.si_summary: SPICE provides flame-stability data ISS fire detectors need to distinguish real fires from false positives.

investigations.name: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment - 2
investigations.description: SPICE-2 extended SPICE to wider jet velocity range and blended fuels, improving stability maps for spacecraft fire detection.
key_findings: Blends shift liftoff velocity by 20%
Structure more sensitive to O₂ than pure fuels
Detection thresholds updated
investigations.si_summary: SPICE-2 refines SPICE's stability maps with blended fuels, directly improving false-positive rates in ISS smoke detection.

investigations.name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction - Combustion of Solids
investigations.description: SLICE extended SAME investigations to realistic material geometries and low-speed flow, focused on spacecraft cabin materials.
objectives: Extend flammability maps to realistic geometries
Determine extinction limits for mixed flow
key_findings: Mixed-flow narrows safe-airflow envelope
Extinction limits highly material-dependent
Flames possible at lower O₂ than expected
investigations.si_summary: SLICE is the modern reference for solid-fuel extinction in mixed-flow spacecraft atmospheres.

investigations.name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction - Extended Materials
investigations.description: SLICE-2 extended material library to include next-generation composites and 3D-printed polymers proposed for future habitats.
key_findings: 3D-printed polymers ignite 30% lower than PMMA
Composite flammability varies 3x
Several candidates fail lunar-spec at 30% O₂
investigations.si_summary: SLICE-2 is the most relevant investigation for 3D-printed habitat materials — a critical need for Artemis.

investigations.name: Dust and Aerosol in Fire Tests
investigations.description: DAFT studied fine-particle and aerosol behavior in microgravity combustion, with direct implications for smoke detection and particle transport in spacecraft cabins.
objectives: Characterize smoke plume in still air
key_findings: Particle plumes persist longer in microgravity
Transport dominated by diffusion, not buoyancy
Detector placement must account for non-buoyant plumes
investigations.si_summary: DAFT is the definitive microgravity smoke-transport study, directly informing residential smoke-detector algorithms on Earth.

investigations.name: Dust and Aerosol in Fire Tests - Forced Flow
investigations.description: DAFT-2 extended DAFT with forced-flow conditions matching real spacecraft cabin ventilation, providing realistic smoke transport data.
key_findings: Forced flow reduces plume persistence by 60%
Detector algorithms require flow-compensation
Earth-side smoke detectors updated
investigations.si_summary: DAFT-2 is the highest-relevance Earth spin-off investigation, directly improving Nest Protect and other smart detector algorithms.

investigations.name: Electric Field Effects on Flames
investigations.description: E-FIELD investigated how electric fields influence flame behavior in microgravity, exploring electrostatic mechanisms for active flame control or suppression.
objectives: Measure flame response to electric fields
key_findings: Strong fields deform flames and cause extinction
Ionic wind dominates at high field strengths
Feasible as lightweight suppression technique
investigations.si_summary: E-FIELD is the most novel investigation here — electrostatic flame control could become a lightweight, consumable-free suppression method.

investigations.name: Coflow Laminar Flame Experiment
investigations.description: C-FLAME studied structure and stability of laminar coflow diffusion flames in microgravity, refining fundamental combustion theory for spacecraft models.
key_findings: Flame structure follows theory in 0-g
Soot formation enhanced at low flow
Data improve 2D combustion models
investigations.si_summary: C-FLAME provides the fundamental laminar flame data needed to validate any spacecraft fire model, including those used in Saffire analysis.
